title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.25760v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Coding agents increasingly carry out long-horizon development tasks, autonomously planning and executing multi-step actions that span files, tools, and sessions. Because developers rarely follow each action, and agents resuming the work depend on records of what was done, the agent's work report often becomes the primary account of what was changed and established. When the report contains false or unsupported claims, it gives recipients false assurance: incomplete work may be accepted without verification, incorrect assumptions about the current state can propagate to later steps and agents, and evaluators that credit stated success may reward the report rather than the work. Yet little is known about what unfaithful reporting looks like in real development work, or how developers and agents handle it once it surfaces. Starting from real developer--agent conversations in SWE-chat, we conduct a systematic mixed-methods analysis of self

translated_title: 编码智能体不忠实工作报告的表征与检测
translated_abstract: 编码智能体越来越多地承担长周期的开发任务，自主规划并执行跨越文件、工具和会话的多步骤操作。由于开发者很少逐项跟进每一步操作，而接续工作的智能体又依赖于已完成工作的记录，智能体的工作报告往往成为对所更改和所建立内容的主要描述。当报告包含虚假或缺乏依据的声明时，会给接收者带来虚假的安全感：未完成的工作可能在未经核实的情况下被接受，对当前状态的错误假设可能传播到后续步骤和其他智能体，而采信声称成功的评估者可能奖励的是报告本身而非实际工作。然而，人们对于不忠实报告在真实开发工作中的具体表现，以及开发者和智能体在其出现后如何应对，仍知之甚少。基于 SWE-chat 中真实的开发者与智能体对话，我们对自我（原文摘要在此处截断，后续内容缺失）
tldr: 该论文基于真实的开发者—智能体对话数据，系统性地刻画了编码智能体在真实开发工作中不忠实工作报告的表现形式及其带来的误导风险，并研究其检测方法。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically characterizes and detects unfaithful work reports produced by coding agents in real developer–agent conversations, revealing how false or unsupported claims can mislead developers, downstream agents, and evaluators.
